scope: Internal paired XTEST pointer-button dispatch, exact RawButton/XKB receipts, retained actual release and WindowFocus integration at the original pixel; mouse business/AT-SPI point integration remains in development.

initial_results.finding: The extra-notification test incorrectly equated all eight owned receipts being complete with absence of interference. Implementation already rejected/latches the extra event. Test now asserts exact expected completion for each fault separately from mandatory latch/rejection; runtime unchanged.

pair_contract.preflight: Revalidate actual point, source, maps, XKB, full pointer configuration and RandR motion plan; prepare precomputed pointer-class transition, then require actual current QueryPointer pixel/root/screen and fully released mask. Reserve both request sequences before first byte; no key/motion/button overlap.
pair_contract.packet: Exactly two36-byte XTEST core ButtonPress4/ButtonRelease5 requests using the actual mapped-plan physical code. Zero delay/root/coordinates/device; no new move, button remapping or layout/configuration write. One object can emit once.
pair_contract.receipts: Eight ordered receipts: RawButtonPress slave/master; XKB source/master ordinary pointer state; RawButtonRelease slave/master; XKB source/master release state. Raw15/16 keeps physical detail on both devices, exact request/source/device/flags0, pair timestamp and no supplied valuators. Extra/missing/out-of-order/mismatched events latch and deny outcome.
pair_contract.xkb: Only paired keyboard StateNotify2, same reserved press/release sequence, changed8192 and no modifier/group/compatibility/grab/lookup state, zero request cause, exact event4/5. Source mask comes from actual slave map (zero above corebutton5), master mask from logical1. Incoming physical/intermediate code normally; mapped code also predicted for press early-return on passive grab. Release uses restored incoming code. No blanket keyboard-state exemption; routing/application success remains external.
pair_contract.source_copy: Reuse the existing full precomputed pointer-copy transition and complete native/configuration/RandR postchecks; final topology/configuration published only after exact receipts and readback. Failure/cancellation cannot clear independent changed latch or adopt provisional state.

release_contract.partial_press: Before full36-byte press, close/drop incomplete stream; never complete a new press merely to clean cancellation.
release_contract.complete_press: After36bytes, retained owner sends only remaining release suffix to72bytes, even after waiter cancellation/interference. Actual write failure keeps lease for later settlement, no press replay.
release_contract.proof: Same-owner QueryPointer barrier requires native valid reply and released five core button bits; then actual XIQueryDevice must prove all enabled physical buttons released and verified source/master still enabled, correct kinds/attachment/button class. Modifiers/root/pixel mismatches may leave action unverified while button release is known.
release_contract.uncertainty: Held logical/physical state keeps actual connection/lease and allows later read-only settlement. A timed-out/incomplete first or second barrier retains original task/stream without replacement queries. Cancelling emit/close waiters cannot cancel owned cleanup. External window/session connection remains with its original owner.

native_configuration: Protocol/socket writes, XKB/source copy and native session all injected. Actual complete WindowFocus/InputWire paths exercised. Fixed HEAD plus own files/import location and root/shadow SHA verified before/after. Default offline gate retained; no environment rebuild or user service stop.
publication: Local-only commit, remote authorization still pending. No push retry.
next: AT-SPI physical-point association and per-action ready/permit plus application result for actual mouse business. Generic provider/navigation, legacy/multiple-root layout, Wayland input and original whole-V2 requirement audit remain open. Full suite only after whole development freeze.
